world.title: Nepal cuts 12 year wait, to declare those missing in flood 'dead' after 45 days
world.summary: Nepal's government has shortened the waiting period for declaring individuals missing in disasters as deceased from 12 years to 45 days. This change affects families of 5,285 missing persons, including at least 189 Indians, following the floods on August 26. The new policy aims to provide closure for families affected by such tragic events more swiftly.

world.title: From India to France: Why are Gen Z students angry?
world.summary: Gen Z students in India and France are expressing anger over poor educational conditions. Following the Cockroach Janata Party's "School Thik Karo" campaign in India, high school students in Créteil, a Paris suburb, initiated protests to draw attention to similar issues in France. Although not directly linked, both movements reflect a shared frustration with inadequate schooling environments.

world.title: Christa Pike, Who Survived Lethal Injection, Returns To US Prison
world.summary: Christa Pike, 50, returned to prison after surviving a botched lethal injection attempt in Tennessee on September 30. She was administered two doses of pentobarbital, which typically results in death, but failed to kill her. Following her discharge from the hospital, her lawyers confirmed her return to prison, where she remains a convicted murderer.

business.title: Rs 22 lakh-crore global green hydrogen boom: 3 stocks eyeing India’s 5 MTPA goal
business.summary: India's green hydrogen initiative, backed by a ₹17,490 crore investment, aims for 5 million tonnes (MTPA) production by 2030 under the National Green Hydrogen Mission. Three companies are strategically positioning themselves to tap into the ₹22 lakh crore global market by enhancing capacity and developing hydrogen projects, aligning with the global shift towards clean energy solutions.

business.title: Emergency Oil Releases Risk Draining the World’s Last Supply Cushion
business.summary: Aramco has cautioned that the global oil supply cushion is critically low, with inventories possibly requiring two years to recover after the reopening of the Hormuz Strait. The International Energy Agency, in collaboration with the G7, announced an additional release of 100 million barrels of oil products, part of a broader plan to release 400 million barrels.

business.title: Will gold prices fall further? Check reasons behind the recent dip, forecasts and more
business.summary: Gold prices have declined significantly in 2026, dropping approximately 5% recently and 13.6% over six months, influenced by rising US bond yields, a stronger dollar, inflation concerns, and profit-taking by investors. As of October 10, spot gold was priced around $4,194.65 per ounce. This decline has prompted investors to reconsider their buying, waiting, or selling strategies.

technology.title: Apple's October 13 Smart Home Event: HomePad, New Apple TV 4K, and LG
technology.summary: Apple will host a significant smart home event on October 13, featuring the HomePad, a 6-inch smart display, and an updated Apple TV 4K. The event aims to enhance its connected home offerings, showcasing various smart home accessories developed in collaboration with LG Electronics. This marks Apple's most substantial initiative in the smart home sector in recent years.

technology.title: ​Malware Embedded in Budget Android Firmware Affects Thousands Worldwide
technology.summary: Researchers have identified Midnight Mimosa malware embedded in budget Android firmware, impacting thousands of devices across 150 countries. This malware operates silently, facilitating ad fraud and proxy abuse. The discovery raises significant security concerns regarding budget smartphones, as the malware is integrated directly into the device firmware, making it difficult for users to detect and remove.

technology.title: Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 review: A familiar design with meaningful upgrades
technology.summary: The Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 features a larger battery, brighter display, and improved fitness capabilities while maintaining its predecessor's rugged design. Priced at Rs 64,999, it includes dual-frequency GPS, LTE connectivity, and new trail-running and hydration-tracking functions. However, limited design changes and lack of iPhone support raise questions about its competitiveness in the premium smartwatch market.

health.title: Combating Cancer among women
health.summary: Dr. Deepak Bharti emphasizes that cancer is no longer viewed as hopeless due to advancements in medical treatments. Innovations in screening, vaccination, surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy have improved the prevention, early detection, and control of many gynaecological cancers. The focus is on reaching women to enhance awareness and access to these life-saving interventions.

health.title: 95% of Alzheimer's Cases Could Be Prevented Through Lifestyle. Neuroscientist Reveals the 3 Free Changes That Protect Your Brain
health.summary: Louisa Nicola, a prominent neuroscientist, claims that 95% of Alzheimer's cases could be prevented through lifestyle changes. In a recent discussion, she highlighted three free modifications that can protect brain health and combat cognitive decline and dementia. Nicola aims to shift public perception regarding brain health and emphasizes the importance of proactive measures for maintaining cognitive function.

health.title: More than just baby blues
health.summary: Postpartum depression can affect mothers regardless of prior mental health issues. The Lindsay Clancy trial, which began in June 2023, highlights this condition's severity. Clancy is accused of killing her three children, with her defense claiming she suffered from severe postpartum psychosis. The case underscores the importance of recognizing both visible and invisible symptoms of postpartum mental health disorders.

science.title: Genetically modified microbe could help make Mars habitable, researchers say
science.summary: Researchers at Pioneer Labs in Emeryville, California, have developed a genetically modified bacterium named sPL.001 that thrives in simulated Martian conditions. This microorganism can break down toxic substances found in Martian soil analogs and produce bioplastics, potentially aiding in the creation of sustainable habitats for future space settlements on Mars.

science.title: Earth
science.summary: A study of WISE 0855, a Jupiter-sized exoplanet 7.5 light-years away, has uncovered atmospheric processes similar to those on Earth and Jupiter. Researchers utilized the James Webb Space Telescope to analyze its weather patterns, revealing that at least two simultaneous processes shape its atmosphere. This discovery enhances understanding of exoplanetary atmospheres and their dynamics.

science.title: Scientists examined a 165-million-year-old fossil from China and found a broad swimming tail plus bony throat structures; the Jurassic mammal predecessor could feed and swallow in ways seen in modern
science.summary: Scientists studied a 165-million-year-old fossil from China, identifying a mammal predecessor with a broad swimming tail and bony throat structures. These features suggest that this Jurassic creature could feed and swallow in ways comparable to modern mammals. The findings provide insights into the evolutionary adaptations of early mammals and their functional similarities to contemporary species.
